interest: Illuminates Japan's postwar diplomatic reemergence, bureaucratic restructuring under Allied Occupation, and the pioneering admission of female diplomats.
keywords: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Establishment Law

overview: This file documents the postwar administrative reorganization of Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and liaison apparatus under Allied Occupation between February 1948 and August 1949. It details the initial abolition of the Central Liaison Office, subsequent consolidation into five bureaus, and the enactment of the 1949 Ministry of Foreign Affairs Establishment Law. The collection also highlights preparations for future trade treaties, the establishment of the Foreign Service Training Institute including the recruitment of female diplomats, and early postwar overseas diplomatic travel.
